name: Sheet-Pan Suppers
summary: One tray, one oven and very little washing up: lemon-oregano chicken with chickpeas and squash, salmon with baby potatoes, harissa cauliflower with lentils and baked eggs, and a fajita tray without the tortillas. Weekday mornings are overnight oats made the night before, and the weekend starts with a sheet-pan egg bake. The carbs are all whole foods.
howItWorks:
**One tray, one oven.** Every dinner roasts on one sheet pan, with whole-food carbs only: potatoes, squash, beans and oats. Weekday trays take about 12 minutes of chopping and 25 to 30 in the oven, and the salmon tray about 35 minutes in all.

**Cook once, eat twice.** Monday's chicken, Wednesday's harissa tray, Thursday's fajita tray and Saturday's meatballs, the one weekend project, each make two portions, so the next lunch is done. Saturday's egg bake is Sunday's breakfast.

**Fish three times.** Salmon on Tuesday, trout on Friday and canned sardines on Saturday carry your omega-3 and some **vitamin D**, which is hard to get from food alone. Fish is never reheated.

**Light.** It covers 1400 to 1800 kcal. It drops one snack a day (both on Thursday) and trims the oats, oil, nuts and seeds, and some of the potatoes, beans, yogurt and meat. The fish, vegetables and fruit stay the same. The chicken and beef trays lean more on chickpeas and vegetables, with a smaller piece of meat, smallest at 1400.

**Big.** It keeps both snacks and grows the meat, fish, eggs, beans, potatoes, oats, yogurt, nuts and oil. The other vegetables and fruit stay about the same. For the two-portion trays, use two pans so nothing crowds.

recipes.name: Berry and walnut overnight oats
recipes.about: Rolled oats soaked overnight in milk and Greek yogurt until creamy, with frozen berries that thaw into a berry swirl and a crunch of walnuts. Five minutes the night before, nothing to cook in the morning, and it brings **protein and fibre** before you leave the house.
steps: Wash your hands. Stir the oats, milk, yogurt and cinnamon together in a jar until there are no dry patches.
Spoon the frozen berries on top, put the lid on and refrigerate overnight. They thaw into the oats and turn them pink, which is what you want.
In the morning, stir it up. If it is thick, loosen it with a splash of milk. Scatter the walnuts on just before eating so they stay crisp.
Keep it in the fridge and eat it within 2 days of making it.
recipes.tip: Make it Sunday night for Monday and Wednesday night for Thursday. At the Big size, use a big bowl or a 1 litre jar. If you are cooking for someone who is pregnant, 60 or older, 5 or under, or has a weak immune system, boil the frozen berries for 1 minute and cool them first, or use fresh.

recipes.name: Apple cinnamon overnight oats with pumpkin seeds
recipes.about: Rolled oats soaked in milk and yogurt with grated apple and plenty of cinnamon, topped with toasted pumpkin seeds. It tastes like apple crisp in a jar, and the seeds bring **iron, zinc and magnesium** along with a good crunch.

ingredients.note: washed and coarsely grated, skin on

steps: Wash your hands and the apple. Grate the apple, skin and all, into a jar.
Add the oats, milk, yogurt and cinnamon and stir until everything is wet and evenly mixed.
Put the lid on and refrigerate overnight. The oats soften and the apple sweetens the whole jar.
In the morning, stir it and loosen with a splash of milk if needed. Top with the pumpkin seeds and eat within 2 days of making it.
recipes.tip: Warm it in the microwave for a minute if you like your oats porridge-style, then add the pumpkin seeds.

recipes.name: Banana walnut overnight oats
recipes.inspiredBy: Inspired by banana bread, in a jar
recipes.about: Overnight oats with mashed banana, cinnamon and walnuts, creamy from Greek yogurt. It tastes like banana bread but gives you **fibre, protein and potassium** to start the day.
steps: Wash your hands. Mash half the banana in a jar until mostly smooth.
Stir in the oats, milk, yogurt and cinnamon until no dry oats remain.
Cover and refrigerate overnight.
In the morning, stir, loosen with a splash of milk if needed, and top with the rest of the banana, sliced, and the walnuts. Eat within 2 days of making it.
recipes.tip: Use a very ripe banana for the sweetest jar.

recipes.name: Sheet-pan sweet potato, spinach and feta egg bake
recipes.inspiredBy: Inspired by a frittata, baked on one tray
recipes.about: A weekend tray of diced sweet potato, red pepper and spinach set in beaten eggs with a little feta and smoked paprika, cut into squares. It makes two breakfasts, and the sweet potato and spinach bring **vitamin A and folate** alongside plenty of protein.

ingredients.note: scrubbed and cut in small dice

steps: Heat the oven to 200 °C (400 °F). Wash the sweet potato, pepper and spinach before cutting. Toss the sweet potato and pepper on a lined sheet pan with the oil, paprika, salt and pepper.
Roast for 15 minutes, until the sweet potato is just tender when poked with a fork.
Scatter the spinach over the tray and push everything into an even layer. Beat the eggs and pour them evenly over the vegetables, then crumble on the feta.
Bake for 12 to 15 minutes, until the eggs are completely set and firm in the centre, with no wet patches. The centre should reach 74 °C (165 °F).
Let it stand for 5 minutes, then cut into squares. Eat half now. Pack the other half in a shallow container within 2 hours and refrigerate.
Reheat the second portion once, until steaming hot, 74 °C (165 °F), and eat it within 3 days.
recipes.tip: A spoonful of plain yogurt on the side cools it down. Roast the sweet potato and pepper the night before and the bake takes about 15 minutes.

recipes.name: Tuna, egg and potato salad with green beans and lemon-parsley dressing
recipes.inspiredBy: Inspired by a French Niçoise salad
recipes.about: Warm little potatoes, crisp green beans, light tuna and a firm hard-boiled egg tossed in a lemony olive oil dressing with tomatoes and spinach. The tuna, egg and white beans bring **protein, choline and B vitamins**, and the whole thing comes together in one pot.
steps: Wash the potatoes, beans, spinach, tomatoes and parsley. Halve any big potatoes so they cook evenly. Cover them with cold water, add the egg in its shell and bring to a boil.
Boil for 10 minutes so the yolk is completely firm. Add the green beans for the last 4 minutes. Lift the egg into cold water, drain the rest and let it steam dry for a minute.
Whisk the olive oil, lemon juice, salt and pepper in a bowl. Toss the warm potatoes, beans, white beans and onion through it so they soak up the dressing.
Peel and quarter the egg. Serve everything over the spinach with the tomatoes, parsley and walnuts, and flake the tuna on top.
recipes.tip: Boil the potatoes and eggs on Sunday night, with 2 extra eggs for Tuesday's snack, and cool them within 2 hours. The potatoes keep 3 days in the fridge, and the eggs keep in their shells for up to 1 week.

recipes.name: Lemon tuna and white bean salad with spinach
recipes.inspiredBy: Inspired by Tuscan tonno e fagioli
recipes.about: Flaked light tuna and creamy white beans over spinach and tomatoes, tossed in lemon and olive oil with red onion and parsley. No pans to wash, and the beans and tuna bring **protein, fibre and iron**, with lemon to help you absorb it.
steps: Wash the spinach, tomatoes and parsley.
Whisk the olive oil, lemon juice, salt and pepper in a bowl. Add the onion and let it sit 5 minutes to soften.
Add the beans, tomatoes and parsley and toss to coat. Flake in the tuna and fold it through gently.
Pile onto the spinach and finish with a crack of pepper.
recipes.tip: Pack the dressed beans and the spinach separately if you are taking it to work.

recipes.name: Sardine and chickpea salad with tomato and lemon
recipes.about: Warm chickpeas tossed with juicy tomatoes, red onion, parsley and lemon, with canned sardines piled on top over spinach. Sardines with their soft bones bring **omega-3, vitamin D and calcium** for almost no effort.
steps: Wash the spinach, tomatoes and parsley. Warm the chickpeas in a small pan or the microwave until hot, 1 to 2 minutes.
Whisk the olive oil, lemon juice, salt and pepper in a bowl. Toss in the warm chickpeas, onion and tomatoes and let them sit for 5 minutes.
Fold in the parsley and pile onto the spinach.
Top with the sardines, broken into big pieces, and squeeze on a little more lemon.
recipes.tip: The tomatoes burst a little as they sit in the warm chickpeas, which makes its own sauce.

recipes.name: Lemon-oregano chicken thighs with chickpeas, squash and red onion
recipes.inspiredBy: Inspired by Greek-style lemon roast chicken
recipes.about: Juicy chicken thighs roasted on one tray with chickpeas, butternut squash and red onion, with garlic, lemon and fresh oregano. The chickpeas crisp at the edges and soak up the pan juices, and the dish brings **protein, fibre and vitamin A**. It makes tomorrow's lunch too.

ingredients.note: peeled and cut in 2 cm chunks

steps: Heat the oven to 220 °C (425 °F). Wash the squash, onion, spinach and oregano before cutting. Toss the squash, onion and garlic on a big sheet pan with half the oil and a third of the salt. Roast for 10 minutes.

Meanwhile, cut the thighs into large pieces so they cook fast, then toss them with the rest of the oil, the lemon juice, half the oregano, the pepper and half the remaining salt. Wash your hands and the board with hot soapy water.

Push the vegetables aside and add the chicken and the chickpeas to the tray, seasoning the chickpeas with the last of the salt. Roast for 18 minutes, until the chicken reaches 74 °C (165 °F) in the thickest part and the squash is tender.
Scatter the spinach over the hot tray and let it wilt for a minute. Finish with the rest of the oregano and spoon the pan juices over everything.
Pack the second portion in a shallow container within 2 hours and refrigerate. Eat it within 3 days, reheated once until steaming hot, 74 °C (165 °F).
recipes.tip: Cut the squash into even chunks so it finishes with the chicken. A spoonful of plain yogurt on the side is lovely. If the pan looks crowded, use two so everything roasts instead of steaming.

recipes.name: Sheet-pan salmon with baby potatoes, white beans, broccoli and lemon-parsley yogurt
recipes.inspiredBy: Inspired by Scandinavian salmon and potatoes
recipes.about: Salmon roasted on one tray alongside crisp little potatoes, white beans and broccoli, finished with a cool lemon, garlic and parsley yogurt sauce. It is about 35 minutes start to finish, and the salmon brings **omega-3 fats and vitamin D**, with iron and fibre from the beans.

ingredients.note: baby potatoes, scrubbed and cut in 2 cm pieces

steps: Heat the oven to 220 °C (425 °F). Wash the potatoes, broccoli, spinach and parsley. Toss the potatoes on a large sheet pan with half the oil and a third of the salt. Roast for 12 minutes.
Meanwhile, stir the yogurt, parsley, garlic, half the lemon juice and a pinch of salt in a small bowl. Keep it in the fridge.
Toss the broccoli with the rest of the oil and push the potatoes to one side. Season the salmon with the rest of the salt and the pepper. Wash your hands and the board after handling the raw fish.

Add the salmon, the beans and the broccoli to the tray and roast for 10 minutes, adding the spinach for the last 2 minutes so it wilts, until the salmon flakes easily and reaches 70 °C (158 °F) and the broccoli is charred at the tips.
Squeeze the remaining lemon juice over everything and serve with the yogurt sauce.
recipes.tip: Swap the salmon for trout or Arctic char.

recipes.name: Harissa cauliflower and lentil tray with baked eggs and feta
recipes.inspiredBy: Inspired by North African harissa roasting
recipes.about: Cauliflower and carrots roasted in a harissa and cumin rub until sweet and charred, tossed with lentils, topped with baked eggs and finished with feta, parsley and toasted almonds. A vegetarian tray with **iron, folate, choline and fibre**, with lemon to help your body absorb the iron. It makes tomorrow's lunch.
steps: Heat the oven to 220 °C (425 °F). Wash the cauliflower, carrots, onion and parsley before cutting. Whisk the harissa, oil, cumin and half the lemon juice in a big bowl with the salt.
Toss the cauliflower, carrots and onion in the harissa mix and spread them on a sheet pan in a single layer. Roast for 20 minutes, turning once, until the edges are charred.

Scatter the lentils over the tray. Make a well in the vegetables for each egg and crack them in, then roast 10 to 14 minutes more, until the whites are set and the yolks are completely firm all the way through. Scatter the almonds on for the last 3 minutes so they toast.
Crumble over the feta and parsley and squeeze on the remaining lemon. Serve with a dollop of yogurt.
Pack the second portion in a shallow container within 2 hours and refrigerate. Eat it within 3 days, reheated once until steaming hot, 74 °C (165 °F).
recipes.tip: Use less harissa for a milder tray, and taste your jar first, since heat varies a lot. If the pan looks crowded, use two so everything roasts instead of steaming.

recipes.name: Fajita chicken tray with peppers, black beans and sweet potato
recipes.inspiredBy: Inspired by Tex-Mex fajitas, without the tortillas
recipes.about: Strips of chicken breast, peppers and onion roasted with smoky fajita spices, with black beans and sweet potato wedges on the same tray. Serve with a quick lime yogurt. It brings **protein, fibre and vitamin C**, and makes tomorrow's lunch.
steps: Heat the oven to 220 °C (425 °F). Wash the sweet potato, peppers, onion and parsley before cutting. Toss the sweet potato cubes with a third of the oil and a pinch of salt on a large sheet pan and roast for 10 minutes.

Mix the chili powder, cumin, paprika, garlic powder and remaining salt. Toss the chicken, peppers and onion with the rest of the oil and the spice mix. Wash your hands and the board after handling the raw chicken.

Add the chicken, peppers, onion and beans to the tray in a single layer, pushing the sweet potato aside. Roast for 15 minutes, until the chicken reaches 74 °C (165 °F) and the edges of the peppers are browned.
Stir the lime juice into the yogurt with a pinch of salt. Squeeze a little lime over the tray too.
Serve with the lime yogurt and the parsley.
Pack the second portion in a shallow container within 2 hours and refrigerate. Eat it within 3 days, reheated once until steaming hot, 74 °C (165 °F).
recipes.tip: Reheat the leftover portion in a hot pan so the edges crisp again.

recipes.name: Sheet-pan trout with sweet potato, broccoli and tahini-lemon sauce
recipes.inspiredBy: Inspired by Middle Eastern fish with tahini
recipes.about: Rainbow trout roasted on one tray with sweet potato and a big pile of broccoli, drizzled with a nutty lemon and garlic tahini sauce. Trout is a mild, tender fatty fish that brings **omega-3 and vitamin D**, and the tahini sauce adds a nutty richness and a little calcium.
steps: Heat the oven to 220 °C (425 °F). Wash the sweet potatoes, broccoli, spinach and parsley. Toss the sweet potato cubes on a sheet pan with half the oil and a third of the salt. Roast for 12 minutes.
Meanwhile, whisk the tahini, half the lemon juice, the garlic, a pinch of salt and 2 to 3 tablespoons of cold water until pourable.
Toss the broccoli with the rest of the oil. Rub the trout with the pepper and a pinch of salt. Wash your hands and the board after handling the raw fish.
Add the broccoli and the trout to the tray and roast for 10 to 12 minutes, adding the spinach for the last 2 minutes so it wilts, until the fish flakes easily and reaches 70 °C (158 °F).
Squeeze the rest of the lemon over the tray, drizzle with the tahini sauce and scatter with the parsley.
recipes.tip: Salmon or Arctic char works here too.

recipes.name: Turkey meatball tray with baby potatoes, white beans and cherry tomatoes
recipes.inspiredBy: Inspired by Italian polpette al forno
recipes.about: Oven-baked turkey meatballs with oats, garlic and parsley on a tray of baby potatoes, white beans, sweet red pepper and cherry tomatoes that burst into a sauce, with spinach wilted in at the end. It is a weekend tray that makes two portions, with **protein, fibre and potassium**.

ingredients.note: baby potatoes, cut in 2 cm pieces

steps: Heat the oven to 200 °C (400 °F). Wash the potatoes, pepper, tomatoes, spinach, parsley and oregano before cutting. Mix the turkey, oats, egg, onion, half the garlic, half the parsley, a pinch of salt and the pepper with your hands. Shape into golf-ball sized meatballs, then wash your hands, the board and any utensil with hot soapy water.
On a large sheet pan, stir the potatoes, whole cherry tomatoes, white beans, pepper, the rest of the garlic, the oregano, the oil and the rest of the salt. Nestle the meatballs in on top.
Bake for 30 minutes, stirring the potatoes once, until the meatballs reach 74 °C (165 °F) in the centre, the potatoes are tender and the tomatoes have burst into a thick sauce.
Stir the spinach and lemon juice through the hot tray so the spinach wilts. Scatter with the rest of the parsley.
Pack the second portion in a shallow container within 2 hours and refrigerate. Eat it within 3 days, reheated once until steaming hot, 74 °C (165 °F).
recipes.tip: Freeze the second portion if you will not eat it within 3 days, then thaw it in the fridge and use within 2 days. If the pan looks crowded, use two so everything roasts instead of steaming.

recipes.name: Beef kofta tray with cauliflower, chickpeas and tahini yogurt
recipes.inspiredBy: Inspired by Middle Eastern kofta and roasted cauliflower
recipes.about: Lean beef kofta spiced with cumin, coriander and cinnamon, roasted with cauliflower, tomatoes and chickpeas and drizzled with a cooling tahini yogurt. A Sunday tray with **iron, zinc and protein**, and the lemon and tomatoes help you absorb the iron.
steps: Heat the oven to 220 °C (425 °F). Wash the cauliflower, tomatoes and parsley before cutting. Toss the cauliflower on a sheet pan with half the oil and a third of the salt. Roast for 12 minutes.

Mix the beef, onion, half the garlic, half the parsley, cumin, coriander, cinnamon and half the remaining salt with your hands. Shape into small fingers or patties, then wash your hands and the board.
Add the kofta, chickpeas and tomatoes to the tray with the rest of the oil and salt. Roast for 12 to 15 minutes, until the kofta reach 71 °C (160 °F) in the centre and the tomatoes have burst.
Whisk the yogurt, tahini, lemon juice and the rest of the garlic with a splash of water. Drizzle over the tray and scatter with the rest of the parsley.
recipes.tip: Make double and freeze the uncooked kofta. Thaw it in the fridge, use within 2 days and never refreeze.

recipes.name: Apple and almonds
recipes.about: A crisp apple with a handful of almonds. The pair gives you **fibre, healthy fats and vitamin E**, and it keeps in a bag all day.
steps: Wash the apple, slice it and serve with the almonds.

recipes.name: Hummus with carrot and pepper sticks
recipes.about: Creamy hummus with crunchy carrot and sweet red pepper sticks. It brings **chickpea protein and fibre**, with vitamin C from the pepper, and needs no cooking.
steps: Wash the vegetables and cut them into sticks and strips. Serve with the hummus for dipping.

recipes.name: Greek yogurt with berries and almonds
recipes.about: Thick yogurt with frozen berries that thaw into a berry sauce and a sprinkle of almonds. It brings **protein and calcium**, and the berries bring vitamin C.
steps: Spoon the yogurt into a bowl and top with the frozen berries. Leave for 5 minutes so they soften, then scatter on the almonds and dust with cinnamon.
recipes.tip: If you are cooking for someone who is pregnant, 60 or older, 5 or under, or has a weak immune system, boil the frozen berries for 1 minute and cool them first, or use fresh.

recipes.name: Spiced roasted chickpeas
recipes.about: Crunchy oven-roasted chickpeas with smoked paprika and cumin. A salty, crisp snack with **fibre and plant protein**.
steps: Heat the oven to 220 °C (425 °F). Pat the chickpeas very dry so they crisp.
Toss them on a small sheet pan with the oil, paprika, cumin and salt.
Roast for 25 minutes, shaking the pan halfway, until crisp and golden. Cool a few minutes, since they crisp up as they cool.
Eat the same day. Stored in a sealed jar they soften within a day or two.
recipes.tip: Roast them on the second shelf while Wednesday's harissa tray or Thursday's fajita tray is in the oven; both run at 220 °C.

recipes.name: Orange and walnuts
recipes.about: A juicy orange with a small handful of walnuts. The orange brings **vitamin C** and the walnuts bring healthy fats and a little omega-3.
steps: Wash the orange, then peel and segment it. Serve with the walnuts.

recipes.name: Banana with walnuts and cinnamon
recipes.about: A ripe banana with chopped walnuts and a dusting of cinnamon. Sweet, soft and crunchy, with **potassium, fibre and a little omega-3**.
steps: Slice the banana into a bowl, scatter over the walnuts and dust with cinnamon.

recipes.name: Hard-boiled eggs with cherry tomatoes
recipes.about: Two firm hard-boiled eggs with sweet cherry tomatoes, black pepper and a squeeze of lemon. It brings **protein and choline** in a snack that travels well.
steps: Cover the eggs with cold water, bring to a boil and boil for 10 minutes, until the yolks are completely firm. Cool in cold water, then peel.
Wash the tomatoes and halve them. Quarter the eggs, add the tomatoes, squeeze on the lemon and finish with the pepper.
Boiled eggs keep in the fridge in their shells for up to 1 week, so make a few at once.
